misconception_description: Student believes that conditional statements, i.e., Python statements that evaluate to either True or False, must be explicitly compared to True or False to be used in conditionals.

solutions.generated_code:
program HapusSpasi
kamus
  s, hasil : string
  i : integer
algoritma
  inputBaris(s)
  hasil <- ""
  for i <- 1 to panjang(s) do
    if (s[i] != ' ') == true then
      hasil <- hasil + s[i]
    endif
  endfor
  output(hasil)
endprogram

metadata.modification_notes: The student rewrote the solution to use a loop-based approach instead of regex so they could apply their understanding of conditionals. They believe that the boolean expression `char.isspace()` must be explicitly compared to False using `== False` to be used in an if statement. From their perspective, this is the proper way to write conditional logic. The code functions correctly despite the redundant comparison, as `(char.isspace()) == False` evaluates to the same boolean value as `not char.isspace()` would.
